newsitem.title: USA: PanEnergy seeks Northeast natgas users.
newsitem.headline: PanEnergy seeks Northeast natgas users.

text.p: PanEnergy Corp said public open season for its Excelsior and Spectrum pipeline projects runs through May 15 to accept requests for capacity.

The Excelsior Pipeline is a New York City access project designed to meet several years of strong historical and forecasted market growth. With a projected in-service date of November 2000, the project will provide 500,000 dekatherms per day of capacity into the New York market.

PanEnergy said Excelsior will create a delivery path into the New York Facilities Group System so that gas supplies can be redistributed within the territories served by Brooklyn Union Gas Co, Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc and Long Island Lighting Co.

PanEnergy said Spectrum is a new pipeline designed to phase-in transport of up to 500,000 dekatherms per day from the Chicago area to growing East Coast markets such as Philadelphia, Newark and New York City. The project also will reach other PanEnergy pipeline markets such as Kansas City and southern Ontario.
The projected initial in-service date is November 1998, with additional capacity available in 1999 and 2000.
"We believe shippers will want to take advantage of PanEnergy's direct access to premium Northeast markets, especially New York City," said PanEnergy.

"The Spectrum project offers cost- effective delivery to these markets and can be phased-in to match demand growth while providing competitive rates at a full range of volumes. Excelsior provides access to multiple upstream supply sources, including Spectrum, while delivering into the New York Facilities Group at a strategic location for future growth."
